scope_note: Maps Indian legal and regulatory obligations to cloud-configuration checks. A passing check is evidence about configuration only; it is not a legal compliance determination. Each obligation says how well its wording has been verified.

check_status.implemented: A rule exists in lambdas/rule_engine/rules/ today.
check_status.planned: Technically checkable via AWS APIs; no rule written yet.
check_status.partial: Only part of the obligation can be checked from configuration.
check_status.manual-only: Cannot be assessed from cloud configuration; must be reviewed by a person.

verification.primary: The wording was read from the official publication on the date in verified_on. See verified_sources and key_points.
verification.secondary: Taken from an official explainer or a third-party reproduction of the text, not the official text itself.
verification.needs-verification: Not read from any official text yet, or sources disagreed.

in_force.upcoming: Notified but obligations not yet binding.

checks.title: Storage not publicly accessible
checks.notes: Covers public S3 buckets and publicly accessible RDS instances. Public snapshots are not checked yet.

checks.title: Encryption at rest enabled
checks.notes: S3 requires SSE-KMS (stricter than the AWS default). EBS, RDS and EFS must be encrypted. DynamoDB is always encrypted by AWS, so it never fails this check.

checks.title: TLS enforced for data in transit
checks.notes: S3 bucket policy must deny aws:SecureTransport=false. ALB HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect is a planned extension.

checks.title: No wildcard Allow on all resources
MFA for IAM users with console access
Root account MFA enabled and no root access keys
checks.notes: Checks the account summary: root MFA enabled and no root access keys. Reading the account summary needs iam:GetAccountSummary.

checks.title: No unused or old IAM access keys
checks.notes: Active access keys at or past POLICYGUARD_KEY_MAX_AGE_DAYS (default 90). The limit is a policy choice, not a legal number.

checks.title: SSH/RDP not open to the internet
VPC flow logs enabled
checks.notes: Flags VPCs in the scanned region with no active VPC-level flow log. Subnet and interface level logs are not counted.

checks.title: S3 server access logging enabled on data buckets
checks.notes: Only buckets tagged handles_personal_data=true are flagged.

checks.title: Logs retained for at least 180 days
checks.notes: Checks CloudWatch log groups only. S3 lifecycle on log buckets is not yet checked. Review which log groups are in scope.

checks.title: Logs retained for at least one year
checks.notes: Checks CloudWatch log groups only. S3 lifecycle on log buckets is not yet checked. Review which log groups are in scope.

checks.title: Log storage located in Indian regions
checks.notes: Checks the S3 bucket and CloudWatch log group that CloudTrail trails deliver to. CERT-In FAQ Q35 says logs may be stored outside India if they can be produced in a reasonable time, so this is a review pointer for most entities; IRDAI and SEBI rules and RBI payment data rules are stricter. Other log destinations are not checked.

checks.title: Data stores located in Indian regions (ap-south-1, ap-south-2)
checks.notes: Checks S3 buckets, security groups, EBS volumes, RDS instances, DynamoDB tables and EFS file systems against ap-south-1 and ap-south-2. Emitted as a review pointer, not a legal finding.

checks.title: Backups configured for data stores
checks.notes: RDS automated backups, DynamoDB point-in-time recovery, EFS automatic backups, and at least one EBS snapshot. AWS Backup recovery points that are not visible as snapshots are not counted, so EBS can over-report.

checks.title: S3 versioning enabled on data buckets
checks.notes: Checks S3 versioning only. RDS/DynamoDB/EBS backups are covered by the planned backup_enabled check.

checks.title: Threat detection and alerting enabled
checks.notes: Checks that a GuardDuty detector is enabled. Alert routing (CloudWatch/SNS) is not yet checked.

checks.title: Retention/lifecycle policy defined for personal-data stores
checks.notes: Only buckets tagged handles_personal_data=true are flagged. Shows a lifecycle rule exists, not that deletion happens when it should. DynamoDB TTL is not checked.

obligations.title: Reasonable security safeguards to prevent personal data breach
obligations.effective_note: Main obligations follow an 18-month transition from the 13 Nov 2025 notification of the Rules (about 13 May 2027). Confirm commencement against the gazette.
applies_to: all data fiduciaries and processors handling digital personal data
obligations.notes: The Act sets the duty; the technical measures are in Rule 6 of the DPDP Rules, listed below.

verified_sources.title: PIB explainer: DPDP Rules, 2025 Notified (November 2025)
verified_sources.how_read: official government press note; an explainer, not the gazette text

key_points: The PIB explainer says failing to maintain reasonable security safeguards carries the highest penalty tier, up to 250 crore rupees.
The Act text itself could not be retrieved (the host blocks automated access), so the wording of section 8(5) is unchecked.

obligations.title: Protect personal data with encryption or equivalent
obligations.notes: Configuration shows encryption is enabled; it does not show key management or tokenisation practice.

verified_sources.title: DPDP Rules 2025 text as reproduced on dpdpa.com (Rules 1, 6, 7)
verified_sources.how_read: third-party reproduction of the rule text; not checked against the gazette

key_points: Safeguards include encryption, obfuscation, masking or virtual tokens, as appropriate.

obligations.title: Control access to computer resources used for processing

verified_sources.title: DPDP Rules 2025 text as reproduced on dpdpa.com (Rules 1, 6, 7)
verified_sources.how_read: third-party reproduction of the rule text; not checked against the gazette

key_points: Appropriate measures to control access to the computer resources used by the fiduciary or its processor.

obligations.title: Visibility on access, logs and monitoring; retain logs and personal data for one year
obligations.notes: How the one-year period interacts with CERT-In's 180 days is a legal question this tool does not decide.

verified_sources.title: DPDP Rules 2025 text as reproduced on dpdpa.com (Rules 1, 6, 7)
verified_sources.how_read: third-party reproduction of the rule text; not checked against the gazette

key_points: Visibility on access to personal data through logs, monitoring and review, to detect, investigate and remediate unauthorised access.
Logs and personal data are retained for one year, unless another law in force requires a different period.

obligations.title: Measures for continued processing despite compromise, such as backups

verified_sources.title: DPDP Rules 2025 text as reproduced on dpdpa.com (Rules 1, 6, 7)
verified_sources.how_read: third-party reproduction of the rule text; not checked against the gazette

key_points: Reasonable measures for continued processing if confidentiality, integrity or availability is compromised, such as data backups.

obligations.title: Notify the Board and affected persons of a breach
obligations.notes: Only the ability to detect a breach can be checked from configuration. The notification itself is a process duty.

verified_sources.title: DPDP Rules 2025 text as reproduced on dpdpa.com (Rules 1, 6, 7)
verified_sources.how_read: third-party reproduction of the rule text; not checked against the gazette

verified_sources.title: PIB explainer: DPDP Rules, 2025 Notified (November 2025)
verified_sources.how_read: official government press note; an explainer, not the gazette text

key_points: Affected people are told without delay, in plain language, with what happened, likely consequences, mitigation and a contact.
The Data Protection Board is told without delay, then given detailed information within 72 hours (longer only if the Board allows on written request).

obligations.title: Erase personal data when purpose is served or consent withdrawn
obligations.notes: Cloud config can show a lifecycle policy exists, not that deletion happens when required. Not verified: the Act text could not be retrieved (the host blocks automated access).

obligations.title: Cross-border transfers allowed except to restricted countries
obligations.notes: The Act permits transfers unless the Government restricts a country, so this is a review pointer, not a violation by itself. Sector rules (RBI, SEBI, IRDAI) can be stricter. Significant Data Fiduciaries may face further localisation requirements. Not verified: the Act text could not be retrieved (the host blocks automated access).

obligations.citation: Consent (s.6), notice (s.5), children's data (s.9), grievance redressal (s.8(10)), processor contracts (s.8(2)), Significant Data Fiduciary duties (s.10)
obligations.title: Obligations that cannot be assessed from cloud configuration
obligations.notes: List these in every report as 'not assessed'. Section numbers here are from memory and must be confirmed. Not verified: the Act text could not be retrieved (the host blocks automated access).

obligations.title: Enable logs for ICT systems and retain them for a rolling 180 days within India
obligations.effective_note: Effective 60 days after 28 April 2022 per the direction text. A later extension for MSMEs was announced (that notice was not read).

verified_sources.title: CERT-In Directions No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In, 28 April 2022
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and read

verified_sources.title: CERT-In FAQs on the Cyber Security Directions (May 2022)
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and read

key_points: All covered entities must enable logs of all their ICT systems and keep them securely for a rolling 180 days, within Indian jurisdiction, and give them to CERT-In with an incident report or on order.
FAQ Q35 says logs may also be stored outside India as long as they can be produced to CERT-In in a reasonable time.
FAQ Q36 says a provider serving users in India must enable and keep financial transaction logs and records in Indian jurisdiction.
FAQ Q37 says the logs to keep depend on the sector and include firewall, IPS, SIEM, web, database, mail, SSH and VPN logs, both successful and unsuccessful events.

obligations.title: Report specified cyber incidents to CERT-In within six hours of noticing them
obligations.notes: Process obligation. PolicyGuard can show alerting exists and could display an incident clock; it cannot file the report.

verified_sources.title: CERT-In Directions No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In, 28 April 2022
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and read

verified_sources.title: CERT-In FAQs on the Cyber Security Directions (May 2022)
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and read

key_points: Cyber incidents listed in Annexure I must be reported to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing them or being told of them.
Annexure I includes unauthorised access of IT systems or data, data breach, data leak, and attacks affecting cloud computing.
FAQ Q31 says the reporting duty applies to all entities, including incidents affecting data held in a third party's systems.

obligations.title: Synchronise system clocks to the specified NTP sources
obligations.notes: Checking this means looking at instance configuration, which PolicyGuard does not do, so it stays manual-only.

verified_sources.title: CERT-In Directions No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In, 28 April 2022
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and read

verified_sources.title: CERT-In FAQs on the Cyber Security Directions (May 2022)
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and read

key_points: ICT system clocks must sync to NTP servers of NIC or NPL, or servers traceable to them. Entities spanning several geographies may use another accurate source that does not deviate from them.
FAQ Q42 says entities relying on native cloud time services may continue to use them.

obligations.framework: RBI payment data storage directions (2018, clarified 2021)
obligations.title: Payment system data stored only in India
applies_to: payment system operators and their service providers
obligations.notes: Reports say RBI's FAQs allow processing abroad if the data is deleted abroad and brought back within one business day or 24 hours. The FAQs were not read.

verified_sources.title: RBI circular RBI/2017-18/153, Storage of Payment System Data, 6 April 2018
verified_sources.how_read: official RBI web page, read in full

key_points: System providers must ensure that all data relating to the payment systems they operate is stored in a system only in India.
For the foreign leg of a cross-border transaction, the data may also be stored in the foreign country if required.
Addressed to authorised payment systems and banks, and issued under section 10(2) read with section 18 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

obligations.title: Data localisation, hosted-service standard and backups for SEBI regulated entities
obligations.notes: Only the CSCRF circular was read. The March 2023 cloud framework body and later clarifications (December 2024, April 2025, August 2025) were not, so check those before relying on this.

verified_sources.title: SEBI CSCRF circular SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113, 20 August 2024
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and searched for the localisation, backup, cloud and compliance-date clauses

key_points: Regulated entities must process and store data within the legal boundaries of India; IT and cybersecurity data sent to a global SOC or SaaS security tools is exempted.
Hosted IT services must be at least equivalent to the MeitY cloud empanelment standard.
Entities must implement, test and maintain data backups and run periodic restoration drills.
Compliance had a glide path: 1 January 2025 for six entity categories with an existing circular, 1 April 2025 for others.

obligations.framework: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines (2023)
obligations.citation: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines v1.0 (April 2023), logging section (page 135 of 175)
obligations.title: ICT infrastructure logs kept for a rolling 180 days within Indian jurisdiction
obligations.notes: A localisation clause for policy and claims data was not found in the text, so data residency is no longer listed here. IRDAI's site also lists a 2026 version of the guidelines; its status was not checked.

verified_sources.title: IRDAI Information and Cyber Security Guidelines, Version 1.0, April 2023
verified_sources.how_read: official PDF, text extracted and searched for the logging and localisation clauses

key_points: ICT infrastructure logs must be kept for a rolling 180 days within the Indian jurisdiction, as per CERT-In directions.
Logs must be protected against tampering and made available to law enforcement, IRDAI, CERT-In and CSIRT-Fin when required.

obligations.framework: IT Act 2000 s.43A and SPDI Rules 2011
obligations.title: Body corporate must maintain reasonable security practices for sensitive personal data
applies_to: body corporates handling sensitive personal data
obligations.notes: Commonly shown through ISO 27001. Expected to be superseded in part as DPDP provisions commence; confirm the transition. Not verified: the statute and rules were not read.
